reviews.body: The 23 focused stateless tests pass with MCP 1.x, but the new compatibility code introduces type-checking failures with supported MCP 2.x dependencies.

review_comments.body:
[P2] Keep the compatibility imports type-checkable with MCP 2.x

With supported MCP 2.x installed (reproduced with 2.2.0), `make lint` fails because `mcp.shared.exceptions` no longer exports `McpError`. Mypy reports `attr-defined` here and in the new test helper; Pyright also rejects the helper import and cannot narrow the return value in `_find_mcp_error`. The 1.x lock masks these failures, but the required [latest-dependency lane](https://github.com/temporalio/ai-integrations/blob/d135820a7ee42d9eb8f0032db92e1c00fe560d87/AGENTS.md#L170-L172) runs lint against newer allowed versions. Make both fallback imports and the error lookup type-check with either MCP major.

comments.body:
The fallback imports now account for the symbol absent in MCP 2.x, matching the existing google_genai compatibility imports. The cause-chain lookup explicitly casts the value after the isinstance check so both alternative imports type-check. Lint and the 23 stateless MCP tests pass with MCP 1.30.0 and with MCP 2.2.0 on the otherwise locked dependencies. With latest dependencies (MCP 2.3.0), the reported import and narrowing errors are gone; a separate mypy error remains at test_google_adk_agents.py:1954 in TypeAdapter(schema).

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
